clue.text: Pluto's bloomer makes a complete failure

parts.note: Dis is another name for Pluto, the Roman god of the underworld
a bloomer is something that blooms, a flower such as the aster

explanation.surface: Someone called Pluto commits a howler that turns out to be a total flop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder that suits 'failure', but it is a flowering plant. Pluto's bloomer reads as Dis's aster.
explanation.definitionFit: A total catastrophe or fiasco is a complete failure.

clue.text: Aim straight

explanation.definitionFit: To aim something is to point it at a target; straight, as in a route with no detours, is the adjective sense.

clue.text: Calm journalist took exam about Europe

indicators.note: about means going round, so the exam word wraps around the journalist

parts.note: sat means took an exam
ED, short for editor, is the crossword's usual journalist

explanation.surface: A newspaper writer stays composed while sitting a test about the European Union.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhurried and composed, so calm in manner.

clue.text: But they won't help you walk on water!

definitions.text: But they won't help you walk on water!

parts.words: But they won't help you walk on water!
parts.note: walking on water sounds miraculous, but the phrase also describes keeping your balance on a rolling ship's deck, which is exactly what this ability does help with

explanation.surface: A wry aside that some limbs fall short of performing miracles.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors with this ability can stay steady on a moving deck, though never actually walk on the sea itself.

clue.text: English study old garden

parts.note: a den is a private room for study or work

explanation.surface: An English student pores over a historic garden.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical garden of Adam and Eve is the original paradise, an ancient garden.

clue.text: Book is short version

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Book is short version (6)' gives IS but nothing builds AIAH; likely cut short or garbled in OCR, and no scan or search gives the full text.

clue.text: Snags or ruins garments

indicators.note: ruins is read as a verb: the letters of the first two words are spoiled and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Snagging or tearing ruins clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Wraparound skirts worn in South-East Asia are items of clothing.

clue.text: Lock up child with horrible irons

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child

indicators.note: horrible suggests the word irons is mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A naughty youngster gets shackled in nasty irons.
explanation.definitionFit: To jail someone is to lock them up.

clue.text: Caine had decorated house in Spain

indicators.note: decorated as in done up, so the letters of the actor's name and the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Michael Caine has had his Spanish villa redecorated.
explanation.definitionFit: A large estate house in Spain or Latin America is called by this Spanish word.

clue.text: Embarrassed about showing effects of sunburn

explanation.walkthrough: 'About' is a link word joining the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Blushing with shame, and literally with a reddened, burnt face from the sun.

clue.text: Capricorn, perhaps, is left back in charge

indicators.note: back tells us the word for left is read backwards

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A star sign is said to be left behind while still being in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capricorn' looks like the star sign, but it names one of Earth's two lines of latitude, as does Cancer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tropic of Capricorn is one of two such lines of latitude, so it is an example.

clue.text: Boat the Poles find moving?

parts.note: Poles looks like people from Poland finding a craft emotional, but it means the long poles a Venetian boatman pushes against the canal bed to propel the boat

explanation.surface: People from Poland find a certain vessel stirring.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian craft propelled by a pole is a boat.

clue.text: Chop allowed for a piece of meat

parts.note: chop means cut
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A butcher has permission to chop up some meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A small slice of lamb or veal, often breaded, is a piece of meat.

clue.text: Use feathers and glue to reduce workforce

parts.note: down is the soft fine feathers of birds
size is a gluey wash used to seal plaster or paper

explanation.surface: Instructions for a craft project involving feathers and adhesive.
explanation.walkthrough: Size is a thin glue-like sealant painters and decorators apply before papering a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Companies that cut staff numbers are shrinking their workforce.

clue.text: Love to have ice-cream outside the Crown

indicators.note: outside puts the ice-cream wrapping around the zero

parts.note: a cornet is an ice-cream cone
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone would love an ice-cream outside a pub called the Crown.
explanation.walkthrough: The Crown is a common British pub name, which is the picture painted; the definition is the ornamental headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: A small ornamental crown worn by nobles is a lesser crown.

clue.text: Very well behaved — virtually getting medal

parts.note: as good as means virtually, practically
a gold is a first-place medal

explanation.surface: A model child is nearly winning a prize for good conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a child who behaves perfectly.

clue.text: Samba I'm playing with right instruments

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are performed in a new order

explanation.surface: Musicians perform a samba with the right instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' shuffles SAMBA, IM and R together to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Xylophone-like percussion with wooden bars are musical instruments.

clue.text: Expert discovered showing great knowledge

parts.note: a pro is an expert
found means discovered

explanation.surface: A specialist is found to be very learned.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep and insightful, displaying considerable learning.

clue.text: Composer from America or Poland can start to arrange broadcast

indicators.note: the start to a word is its first letter
broadcast as in scattered widely, so the letters are spread and rearranged

explanation.surface: An American composer's work is arranged for broadcast in Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From America' looks like it supplies an A, but it belongs to the definition, an American composer; the extra A comes from 'start to', and 'broadcast' makes ARONCOPLAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Copland wrote Appalachian Spring and was a leading twentieth-century US composer.

clue.text: Managed to turn up and see judge tell a story

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means reading the word from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
rate means judge or assess

explanation.surface: Someone manages to appear and watch a judge recount events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To turn up' reverses RAN to NAR; 'and see' are padding joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount events is to tell a story.

clue.text: Gran's extremely cold in this fabric

parts.note: nan is a familiar name for a grandmother
a keen wind is bitingly cold

explanation.surface: Grandma is freezing in this flimsy material.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellowish cotton cloth originally from Nanjing is a fabric.

clue.text: See what water is after it thaws

parts.words: what water is after it thaws
parts.note: once frozen water has melted, it is no longer frozen, so the phrase reads as two words meaning the opposite of frozen

parts.words: what water is after it thaws
parts.note: once frozen water has melted, it is no longer frozen, so the phrase reads as two words meaning the opposite of frozen

explanation.surface: A riddle about what melted water becomes.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as two words: thawed water is 'not ice'.
explanation.definitionFit: To see something is to spot or observe it.

clue.text: Reverend looks up to German church official

indicators.note: in a down clue looking up means reading the abbreviation from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A vicar admires a German churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: A church caretaker who also leads processions is a church official.

clue.text: Grass on firmer ground

indicators.note: ground as in crushed or milled, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Turf laid on harder soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like lawn, matching 'ground', but it is slang for a police informer, and 'ground' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a grass is someone who tells tales to the police.

clue.text: In business this setter makes salary

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of earning a good wage in commerce.
explanation.definitionFit: Regular earnings from work are one's income.

clue.text: Spot the spy

explanation.definitionFit: A small dark blemish on the skin is one sense; a double agent planted inside an organisation is the other.

clue.text: Stop outside dwelling in kingdom near China

indicators.note: outside puts the word for stop around the dwelling

parts.note: ban means stop or prohibit
a hut is a simple dwelling

explanation.surface: Banning shacks in a Himalayan land.
explanation.definitionFit: A Himalayan kingdom bordering China and India is a kingdom near China.

clue.text: Chap with phone acting as a reporter

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a chap or fellow
ring means phone

explanation.surface: A man with a telephone is doing the job of a journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: A journalist covering a story is reporting on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Reporting on an event, as journalists do when they cover a story.

clue.text: Second snake is more blue

parts.note: an adder is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: A second serpent is even more depressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue means unhappy, so more blue is unhappier.

clue.text: It's said water is expensive for Rudolph, say

indicators.note: it's said marks that the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: rain is water falling from the sky; dear means expensive

explanation.surface: A complaint that water costs too much, with a Christmas character tagged on.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolph is the famous red-nosed one pulling Santa's sleigh, an example of the species.
